docs.purpose: Where an administrator turns on two-factor sign-in for their own account. It shows whether a authenticator app is already registered, walks through adding one by displaying a setup code to scan and asking for the six digits back to prove it worked, and then shows a set of one-time backup codes. The setup code and the backup codes are shown exactly once - leaving the screen loses them for good. It also allows removing a registered device behind a confirmation.
docs.data_story: It reads nothing from the database directly. Every value arrives through 2 contracts: `/api/admin/security/mfa`, `/api/admin/security/mfa/verify`. Behind those contracts, the data comes from `admin_backup_codes`, and writes land on `admin_audit_log` and `admin_backup_codes`.
docs.under_126: **REBUILD** — it drives writes, so a client decision has to be re-homed on the server before the projection can be honest. It renders through the FORM renderer (every field carrying its Spec 99 §3 ownership row as data, with a declared rollback), reading by reference: `/api/admin/security/mfa`, `/api/admin/security/mfa/verify`. It owns no component of its own, so its `owns.components[]` is an empty array — a legal answer, written down.

versioning.why: The enroll/verify/unenroll sequence is pinned by the GoTrue factor lifecycle on one side and the ten-row admin_backup_codes contract on the other; a shape change here forces a re-enrolment of every admin, so it is not a one-commit change.

inputs.why: Factor status, enrolment and verification all arrive through the two MFA contracts; the page reads no table and holds no server data of its own.

outputs.why: Every step is a server round-trip that must succeed before the UI advances — GoTrue issues the factor, the verify call upgrades the session to aal2, and the ten backup codes are written in one transaction. Nothing flips optimistically, because a wrong guess here locks an operator out.
outputs.rollback: DELETE /api/admin/security/mfa unenrols the factor and deletes the backup codes, writing an mfa_unenrolled audit row. There is no rollback for the one-time material itself: the QR secret and the ten codes exist only in component state and are gone irrecoverably on unmount.

state.why: Factor status is a TanStack query at 10s staleTime; the one-time enrolment material is deliberately NOT in the cache — it lives in component state so it cannot be rehydrated from IndexedDB after the operator leaves the page.

staleness.why: 10s staleTime — short, because the page must reflect an enrolment that just happened in the same session rather than a cached "not enrolled".

session.why: There is no admin Postgres role: classifyRoute sends every /admin/* path down the admin arm, and the real boundary is verifyAdminAuth reading profiles.is_admin on the route. All four handlers verify AND additionally require authMethod === "session", so neither the CI token nor the break-glass key can enrol, verify or unenrol a factor. verifyAdminAuth also becomes an aal2 check here once ADMIN_MFA_ENFORCED is true.

rls_class.why: admin_audit_log is one of the two admin-identity Class-A tables (admin_uid-keyed, is_admin-gated, read-only); admin_backup_codes is outside the named ten, so Class B by the §2 default.

guards.flag: ADMIN_MFA_ENFORCED — when true, verifyAdminAuth additionally requires aal2 or a consumed backup code on every admin route

checks.why: All four handlers refuse any credential that is not a real session, so a CI token cannot enrol or unenrol a factor — a pre-request gate, not an assertion after the fact.
Completing enrolment writes mfa_enrolled and unenrolling writes mfa_unenrolled to admin_audit_log; this is one of only two surfaces in the shard whose mutations land an audit row at all.
The QR secret and the ten backup codes must never enter the query cache, because the root provider persists that cache to IndexedDB for 24 hours.
A wrong TOTP code must render inline and leave the factor pending rather than dropping the operator back to an unenrolled screen; the admin-security UI suite locks the sequence.

errors.why: The mutation hooks raise sonner toasts on failure and the page keeps the step it was on; a failed status read renders inline instead.

classes.ui: toast — wrong or expired TOTP code; the factor stays pending
toast — a non-session credential is refused

emits.why: Three admin_action_performed events fire from the hooks (enroll started, verify attempted, unenroll) and two of the three server actions additionally write an admin_audit_log row.

offers.why: An internal operator tool renders no sponsored placement; no offers/placements table is reached from any file it owns.

metering.why: Nothing here is billable or quota-bearing: no usage_events / ledger write is reached from this surface or its contracts.

config.why: Its one switch, ADMIN_MFA_ENFORCED, is an environment variable rather than a registered logic variable, so there is no bounded tunable to declare.

sharing.why: Both MFA contracts have exactly one caller — this page's hooks in src/features/admin-security.

limitations.measured: Only the paired verify POST writes mfa_enrolled; starting an enrolment leaves no admin_audit_log trace of its own.

limitations.what: The audit write is not transactional with the act it records
limitations.measured: Both writeAdminAudit calls sit in a try/catch whose failure is logged and swallowed, so an unenroll can succeed with no audit row.

limitations.what: Responses carrying one-time secrets set no Cache-Control: no-store
limitations.measured: The enroll response returns the TOTP secret and URI and the verify response returns ten plaintext backup codes; neither sets a no-store header.

limitations.what: Five of the eight measured UI states have no member in the states[] vocabulary
limitations.measured: not_enrolled, enrolling, verifying, backup_codes_shown and confirm_unenroll are real render branches; the closed set offers none of them.
limitations.check_id: none — vocabulary gap, escalated per Spec 128 §4

limitations.what: touch_target_min_px has no legal answer for a desktop-only admin page
limitations.measured: The schema allows only UNRESEARCHED or an integer >= 44, and nothing in this surface declares a 44px floor (grep for min-h-[44 / h-11 over its owned files returns nothing).
limitations.check_id: none — vocabulary gap, escalated per Spec 128 §4

notes: Spec from the page's own SPEC LINK (13_authentication.md Sec 3.6, the MFA gate); the file appears in no system-map row. /api/admin/security/mfa carries GET (status), POST (enroll) and DELETE (unenroll, factor_id in the query string); /api/admin/security/mfa/verify is the POST confirm. One-time material is held only in local component state, never in the query cache - unmount discards it irrecoverably. The hooks live in src/features/admin-security/, outside src/components/, so excluded from files per the stated rule. identity.owner is UNRESEARCHED estate-wide: no owner registry exists in the tree, so naming one would be an invention rather than a measurement. a11y.touch_target_min_px is UNRESEARCHED because its vocabulary (UNRESEARCHED or an integer >= 44) has no member for a desktop-only admin page that declares no floor.

measured_gate.why: classifyRoute('/admin/security') matches the admin-pages arm via `pathname.startsWith('/admin/')` -> 'admin'. The page's own header comment additionally states each API call behind it runs verifyAdminAuth plus a session-mode check.

programme.why: An admin surface that operates the PLATFORM (users, entitlements, security, tunables, pipeline health) rather than either product specifically.
